source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Axiomatic design (AD) has four domains: customer, functional, physical, process. Two axioms: keep functional requirements (FRs) independent; minimise information content. The design matrix A in FR=[A]DP is diagonal (uncoupled), triangular (decoupled) or otherwise coupled.
numbers: No numbers. Matrix classes: diagonal = uncoupled, triangular = decoupled, other = coupled.
quote: Maintain the independence of the functional requirements (FRs).
limits: Secondary account grounded in Suh books; the author is an AD advocate.
agent_relevance: Independence axiom as a cheap code check: write the FR-by-DP matrix and test if it is triangular. The program, not the model, can do this (G5).

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: The axioms can only be applied after the first-level FRs exist. They are deductive tools that grade a design. They do not tell you how to turn needs into FRs, which is inductive or abductive work.
numbers: No numbers. Paper says problem formulation is the most critical and most error-prone AD step, citing Suh.
limits: Argument, not experiment. Relies on Suh page citations.
agent_relevance: Matches our schema: checks run on a restated problem but cannot create it. The restate step needs a separate source of quality.

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Suh theorem S3 as cited: if first-level FRs are wrong, no lower-level design decision can repair it. Coupling introduced at the top propagates through the whole decomposition and raises information content and complexity.
numbers: Cites Suh complexity theory (2005) p. 48; no measured data.
limits: Claim from theory; no empirical test found in this paper.
agent_relevance: Supports a guardrail to freeze and double-check the top-level problem restatement before decomposing. Testable: inject a wrong top-level FR and see if downstream checks catch it.

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Zigzagging: alternate between what (FR) and how (DP) domains, writing the design equation at each level so the independence axiom is checked at every level. Essential FRs are solution-neutral; derived FRs depend on chosen DPs and system constraints.
numbers: Example: tank-level FR written as one FR with design range 10 ms to 50 ms. Vehicle essential FRs: go forward, backward, stop, turn. Flying object: lift, thrust, maneuver.
limits: Illustrations only.
agent_relevance: Zigzag is a decomposition operator with a built-in check per level. Compare to our operators O1-O8: decompose, verify independence, recurse.

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Paper claims LLMs do well at induction, increasingly at deduction, but struggle with abduction, so chatbots help with design parameters and derived FRs but often fail to give the essential FRs. It cites ARC results and a Zahavy 2026 note.
numbers: No measurements by the author. Claim is argued, not tested.
quote: LLMs can help with DPs and derived FRs but fall short at essential FRs.
limits: Opinion in a short section. No LLM was run. Treat as a hypothesis, not evidence.
agent_relevance: Hypothesis for a test: give an LLM customer needs and score whether its first-level FRs match expert FRs and are mutually independent. No such study found.

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Example failure: rewriting "make a call" as "make a call over electromagnetic waves" bundles a solution choice into an FR and breaks independence. Paper says LLMs can easily copy this poor formulation.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Single hand-picked example.
agent_relevance: A lint rule on FR text: no means words inside a requirement. Code-checkable by a separate pass looking for solution words (G3, G5).

source: Homay (2026) critique of Liu on FR variation
finding: Homay disputes Ang Liu: for fixed needs, first-level FRs should not vary between designers; only solutions and lower-level FRs vary. He says no statement in Suh three books allows legitimate first-level FR variation.
numbers: Liu cancer example: biological, pharmaceutical or public-health framings. Homay says these are DPs, not FRs.
limits: An open dispute inside AD. Nobody has tested inter-designer agreement on first-level FRs.
agent_relevance: Our G4 says same-model samples are not independent. FR agreement across samples is a measurable proxy: sample N restatements, compare FR sets.

source: Giordano et al. (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: the case of axiomatic design theory (ICED25)
finding: First annotated benchmark of AD concepts in text: 6,000 patent sentences, annotated by two experts for FR (Doer, Action, Receiver), DP, and axiomatic relations (the design matrix entries). It is a dataset paper; no LLM was scored yet.
numbers: 14,417 US patents; 4,408,204 sentences; 2,929,742 after length filter 10-40 words and dedup; 750 sentences per IPC section A-H gives 6,000. 19,555 annotated concepts total.
limits: Dataset and agreement study only. LLM benchmark results are future work.
agent_relevance: Shows AD concepts can be put into a labelled test set. Useful if we build an FR/DP extraction check.

source: Giordano et al. (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: the case of axiomatic design theory (ICED25)
finding: Counts of annotated concepts show FRs are common but explicit links from a DP to an FR are rare.
numbers: FR 5,019 (0.84 per sentence); DP 3,169; Action 4,372; Doer 2,861; Receiver 4,009; axiomatic relation 878; relation pointer 234. Sentences with explicit relation 226 (3.77%), implicit 410 (6.83%), no FR or DP 2,480 (41.33%).
limits: Patent text only; verb-form FRs and noun-form DPs only.
agent_relevance: Dependencies between requirements are mostly implicit in text. A model must infer the design matrix, which is where independence checks would go wrong.

source: Giordano et al. (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: the case of axiomatic design theory (ICED25)
finding: Two experts agree only moderately on AD concepts. Agreement is lowest for the function requirement as a whole and for the relation.
numbers: F1 between annotators: Action 0.80, Receiver 0.68, Doer 0.66, DP 0.66, AXR 0.57, AXP 0.55, FR 0.52. Face-validity errors 161 of 19,555 (0.8%).
limits: Two annotators, F1 vs one gold annotator; no kappa. Guidelines were revised every 600 sentences.
agent_relevance: Human ceiling for FR and DP-FR relation labelling is about 0.5 to 0.6 F1. An LLM judged against one human label cannot be trusted above that. Prefer code-based checks.

source: Giordano et al. (2025) Decoding the grammar of design theory for LLMs: the case of axiomatic design theory (ICED25)
finding: Prior LLM and NLP work on AD concepts was tiny and mostly unscored: Li and Tate 2010 used 15 FR-DP pairs from two patents; Akay and Kim 2020 used 2 FRs and 4 DPs (faucet, refrigerator); Akay and Kim 2021 used 88 FR-DP pairs from 11 abstracts with BERT question answering.
numbers: Prompts quoted: "What is the aim?" for FR, then "How does it {FR}?" for DP. Akay et al 2023 built an LLM chatbot extracting FR and DP from specs.
limits: Described in the Giordano paper; the original papers were not opened.
agent_relevance: The LLM-for-AD literature measures extraction of FR/DP from text. None found measures whether an LLM can keep FRs independent.

source: Dong et al. (2026) AssemCAD: production-ready CAD assembly generation from natural language
finding: Uses 62 engineering "axioms" (rules like clearance fit, gear module match) that every mate must cite. NOT Suh axiomatic design. Name clash. Still a case of a typed spec plus code verifier beating raw LLM code.
numbers: ASSEMBENCH 120 assemblies. Text-to-CAD success / assembly preservation: AssemCAD 89.17 / 87.50. GPT-5.5 79.17 / 66.67; Qwen3.7-Max 78.33 / 39.17; Claude-4.8 85.00 / 0.83.
limits: No ablation found; assembly preservation judged by an LLM code judge (score 4 of 5 or more) and a VLM. Axioms are textbook rules, not independence of FRs.
agent_relevance: Keep out of the AD count. Useful as evidence that code that runs is not code with the right structure: 85% success but 0.83% preservation for one frontier model.

source: Dong et al. (2026) AssemCAD: production-ready CAD assembly generation from natural language
finding: Image-conditioned setting and backbone swap results.
numbers: Image-text: AssemCAD 84.17 / 82.50; GPT-5.5 79.17 / 64.17; GLM-5.2 76.67 / 40.83; Claude Opus 4.8 65.83 / 0.00; Gemini 3.5 Flash 30.83 / 0.00. Backbone swap: Claude-4.8 preservation 0.8 to 82.50; GPT-5.5 64.2 to 71.67.
limits: Overall quality scores computed only on successful examples. LLM judges.
agent_relevance: A deterministic verification layer lifted a weak backbone from near 0 to 82.5 on this benchmark. Supports G5: code selects and checks.

source: Yoong, Palleti, Silva, Poskitt (2020) Towards systematically deriving defence mechanisms from functional requirements of cyber-physical systems
finding: Uses AD-style decomposition on a water treatment plant testbed (SWaT) to derive invariants (checkable rules) for attack detection. Top level is a diagonal (uncoupled) matrix of 8 FRs and 8 DPs.
numbers: 8 high-level FRs decomposed to 30 FRs at level 2 and 44 concrete FRs overall. Two invariants implemented as decision trees; both attack tests were detected, no false positives reported.
limits: Position paper. Two attacks only. The authors add an information-state coupling that goes beyond Suh physical coupling. No baseline.
agent_relevance: A real use of AD matrices to generate runtime checks. Maps to our idea: derive invariants from the task spec, then check outputs against them.

source: Yoong, Palleti, Silva, Poskitt (2020) Towards systematically deriving defence mechanisms from functional requirements of cyber-physical systems
finding: Authors extend the design matrix with state coupling (dependence by information state, not by physical structure). The matrix is then no longer cleanly triangular, and they note it is symmetric.
numbers: Example: valve DP7 depends on FR1 (pump on), FR2 (tank low), FR7. Number of state equations grows as 2^n for n components, so they use decision trees to generalise.
limits: Exponential growth in hand-written equations.
agent_relevance: Boundary of the theory: independence is clean for physical structure but hard for behaviour that depends on state. Software and LLM steps are state-dependent.

source: Sandhu et al. (2024) Multi-objective aerodynamic optimization of an external-compression supersonic intake using Kriging/MOGA
finding: AD used to set up an optimisation: two objectives (pressure recovery, drag) forced two design parameters by merging three ramp angles into one Oswatitsch triplet. The matrix is lower triangular with one weak off-diagonal term.
numbers: Total pressure ratio of the diffuser 0.885 to 0.907 for the modified design; mass flow ratio 0.955 to 0.983. Authors say the matrix is not strictly AD-conformant because of the small element.
quote: Maintain the independence of the functional requirements.
limits: AD only frames the formulation. The gains come from the new geometry and the genetic algorithm, not from AD. No test without AD.
agent_relevance: Shows the rule "as many DPs as FRs" can be met by bundling variables. Credit for results is not isolatable to the axiom.

source: Sandhu et al. (2025) Tradeoffs in biconic intake design with sub-optimal Oswatitsch solutions
finding: Same group, same AD guidelines: minimise objectives, keep them independent, as many DPs as objectives, aim for diagonal then triangular matrix. Writes TPR and drag as lower triangular in cone angle pair and fineness ratio.
numbers: Two objectives, two DPs after merging three parameters; fineness ratio has a weak effect on TPR.
limits: Again no AD-versus-no-AD comparison.
agent_relevance: Typical pattern in the field: AD is a formulation checklist, rarely tested as a cause of better outcomes.

source: Qiang et al. (2026) Systematic comparison of building ontologies (arXiv 2603.14374)
finding: False friend: "axiomatic design" here means logical axioms in ontologies, scored with the OQuaRE framework, not Suh. Haystack scored 4.25, Brick 3.93, RECore 3.91, DB 3.60 overall.
numbers: Scores on a 1 to 5 scale; DB reliability 2.88.
limits: Not Suh axiomatic design; exclude from AD evidence.
agent_relevance: Flag so later agents do not count it.

source: Khayal and Farid (2019) Dynamic system model for personalized healthcare delivery
finding: Builds a model on hetero-functional graph theory, which Farid derived from axiomatic design for large flexible engineering systems, plus Petri nets. AD is a root of the formalism, not a tested claim.
numbers: No AD-specific numbers.
limits: Two illustrative case studies; no test of the independence axiom.
agent_relevance: Example of AD ideas migrating into graph formalisms. Low value for our schema.

source: Wikipedia: Axiomatic design
finding: Gives the two axioms, FR=A x DP, and says coupling means one DP strongly moves two FRs. Says Suh (MIT) developed it from the 1990s. Lists books: Suh 1990, 2001, 2005; El-Haik 2005; Stamatis 2002. Says it addresses issues in Taguchi methods.
numbers: ICAD conferences listed 2000 to 2021.
quote: Maintain the independence of the functional requirements (FRs).
limits: Encyclopedia summary; lacks theorems and information formula.
agent_relevance: Basic citation anchors only.

source: Suh (1995) Axiomatic design of mechanical systems (J. Mechanical Design)
finding: Abstract (read via Crossref) states key concepts: domains, characteristic vectors, zigzagging hierarchies, two axioms, and corollaries and theorems for simple systems, large systems and organisations. Claims all design fields share a common thought process.
numbers: No numbers in abstract. Crossref lists 56 citations.
limits: Only the abstract was read; paywalled.
agent_relevance: Foundational statement that design rules can be derived from two axioms; not tested empirically in the abstract.

source: Suh (1998) Axiomatic design theory for systems (Research in Engineering Design)
finding: Extends axioms to large systems and gives theorems. Metadata only; text not opened.
numbers: About 433 citations (Crossref, 2026).
limits: Paywalled; no abstract in Crossref.
agent_relevance: Key primary to read if access is found.

source: Suh (1999) A theory of complexity, periodicity and the design axioms (Research in Engineering Design)
finding: Links design axioms to a complexity theory. Homay (2026) cites Suh for imaginary complexity: uncertainty that comes from the designer lack of knowledge, not from the system. Original not opened.
numbers: About 137 citations (Crossref).
limits: Paywalled; only metadata opened.
agent_relevance: Complexity as a measure could be a cheap proxy for coupling in a plan.

source: Hazelrigg (1999) An axiomatic framework for engineering design (J. Mechanical Design)
finding: Rival normative view: design is decision making under uncertainty. Eight axioms yield two theorems, and a third theorem imposes severe conditions on design methodologies. Gives results that differ from conventional design analysis on a simple example.
numbers: 8 axioms, 3 theorems; about 59 citations.
limits: Only the abstract was read. The abstract does not name Suh.
agent_relevance: Competing frame: choose designs by expected utility, not by independence. Fits our G5 code-selected ranking.

source: Dubois, Tate et al. (2012) Comparing strategies and outputs of designers using TRIZ/AIPS, Axiomatic Design or Environment-Based Design
finding: Found by Crossref: a comparative study of designers using AD against other methods. Only the title and authors were seen. Result unknown.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Paywalled (HTTP 403). Do not use any result.
agent_relevance: Lead for angle B: the one comparison study of AD users I found.

source: Kulak et al. (2005) Fuzzy multi-attribute equipment selection based on information axiom
finding: Example of the information axiom used as a selection rule for equipment. Not opened.
numbers: About 163 citations (Crossref).
limits: Metadata only.
agent_relevance: Information axiom as a ranking rule: pick the option with the highest chance of meeting the range. Matches our selection idea.

source: Suh (background): information axiom and design matrix classes
finding: From background knowledge, not verified here: information content I=log2(1/p), where p is the chance the design meets the FR (common range over system range). Prefer uncoupled over decoupled over coupled.
numbers: No numbers verified.
limits: Unverified recall. Do not cite as established until opened.
agent_relevance: If kept: selection among candidate plans by estimated success probability fits G5 only when the probabilities come from code, not from the model.

source: Gap statement (this search)
finding: Giordano et al. say earlier LLM work on AD lacked quantitative scoring against the theory definitions. My own search (arXiv, Crossref) found no 2020-2026 study that gives an LLM a task and scores whether it keeps FRs independent or builds a correct design matrix.
numbers: arXiv phrase search "axiomatic design" returned 6 papers, 1 touching LLMs (Homay 2026). Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate-limited; WebSearch budget was used up.
limits: Absence of evidence after a limited search. Could miss journal papers.
agent_relevance: A real gap. A small test of LLM independence checks on a design matrix would be new data.
